# PLAN — iteration 3
## Current state assessment
The verified incumbent is already timing-feasible at 7 LUTs and 9 FFs, so this iteration must strictly reduce LUTs without losing setup or hold closure. Iterations 1 and 2 both used an 8-bit counter and were rejected: each passed behavioral and timing checks but mapped to 10 LUTs. The current top’s numeric latency is unknown, so no numeric latency annotation is required.

## Hypothesis
Writing the modulo-256 increment as explicit per-bit toggle logic may let Vivado map the counter update with fewer LUTs than the previously tried increment expressions.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the 32-bit counter with an 8-bit counter and replace the terminal-count branch and `counter + 1` update with explicit toggle equations: bit 0 toggles every enabled cycle, and each higher bit toggles when all lower bits are one. Preserve synchronous reset of the counter and `pwm_out`, and keep the registered comparison `pwm_out <= (counter < duty)` using the pre-update counter value. This is a new RTL coding pattern, but the behavior is still modulo-256 counting; retain it only if all gates pass and routed LUT use is strictly below 7.
